tasks.title: UTRAnnotator uORF class picked by hash order (PRED-15)
tasks.desc:

The plugin is the shared copy in /data_lab_PGP/resources (not this repo's), so this starts with your choice:

(b) accept and document the instability.

Source: BUG_TRACKER.md PRED-15; walkthrough/20261104_utrannotator_high_impact_grading.md.

notes.text: Self-contained description (Mario: board informative)

Question: PRED-15: (a) fork UTRAnnotator into this repo and make it emit every uORF class deterministically, or (b) accept and document the instability? I recommend (a): the instability flips high_impact/other on real rows (6 of 1,780 shared rows), and a pinned in-repo copy also helps RP-01.
Mario chose (a): fork UTRAnnotator into this repo and make it emit every uORF class deterministically.

Done locally (uncommitted): this repo now has its own copy of the plugin, src/external/vep_plugins/UTRAnnotatorPGP.pm, which reports every uORF class of a variant in a fixed order. Each 5UTR_annotation entry says which class it belongs to, and UTRAnnotator_status grades every class.
- Checked: the plugin compiles in the VEP container and gives identical output under 8 Perl hash seeds; the old selection loop gave a different class across those seeds. All 51 Python test modules pass.
- Left: two cluster runs of a 34-variant fixture (the variants whose class differed between F2005_union and F1830_union_avi), then src/tools/compare_utr5_runs.py. Commands and pass criteria: walkthrough/20261110_utrannotator_deterministic_fork.md.

tasks.title: Investigate SpliceAI2 and its inclusion
tasks.desc: New predictor, an update from SpliceAI: SpliceAI was just launched. Check how can we implement it in our pipeline

notes.text: Plan: find the primary source (paper/preprint, code, weights, licence, genome build, precomputed scores), compare with SpliceAI 1.3.1 as wired here (gene-restricted tier, -D 4999, score cache), and write a short inclusion memo with options. No code change until you choose.

SpliceAI2 can go in as an informational score; it cannot replace SpliceAI for ACMG. Memo: walkthrough/20261106_spliceai2_inclusion.md (faffd93).
- Recommended route (A): Illumina's precomputed GRCh38 scores (all SNVs + ~150M population indels, protein-coding genes) looked up like ReMM/AVI, with a status column. Live scoring needs CUDA GPUs; our SpliceAI runs on CPU.
- SpliceAI stays the PP3/BP4 predictor: only it has ClinGen-calibrated thresholds; SpliceAI2's benchmarks are all by the developers (preprint, no independent evaluation yet).
Your decisions before any code:
1. Licence: non-commercial research only, no redistribution. Does it cover reports to families, and tables shared outside the lab? -> YES
2. Accept the Hugging Face gate (personal account) so I can see the size/format of precomputed_scores_v2.0 (~350 GB for the whole dataset). -> OK
3. Does the cluster have GPU nodes? Only matters for option B (scoring private indels). -> yes it has but go with route A
Implementation is proposed separately as PR-03.

tasks.title: Step 6: were past SpliceAI failures silent?
tasks.desc:
Why: before PRED-16 the SpliceAI wrapper swallowed every per-record error and wrote the site unscored. The old cache (ca2807064ffcf846) has 389,061 unscored sites; if many of them get a score with the fixed code, past runs silently lost SpliceAI scores.

State: the new cache version (68a43b063014889b) holds only the migrated scored sites; no run has rescored the unscored ones yet.

To do: I build a VCF of a random sample (about 2,000) of those unscored sites, seeded and recorded; you launch a short run with the test cache; I count how many now carry a score, and from which genes.

Done when: a rate (scored / sampled) with the run name. 0 = no evidence of silent failures; otherwise a note on which past tables are affected.
Source: TODO.md checklist step 6.

notes.text: Plan: sample about 2,000 sites the old SpliceAI cache left unscored (seeded, recorded), build a fixture VCF, hand over the launch command, then count how many get a score.

Input ready: test_data/raw_vcfs/spliceai_unscored_sample.vcf.gz holds 2,000 sites drawn at random (seed 20261110) from the 377,321 positions the old SpliceAI cache left without a score; 1,968 of them reach SpliceAI. Command for Mario (pending):
bash run_annotate_vcf.sh -profile standard --input_vcf test_data/raw_vcfs/spliceai_unscored_sample.vcf.gz --annotation_cache_dir /mnt/scratch/mruizp/annotation_cache_test --run_id spliceai_unscored_sample_20261110

No evidence of silent SpliceAI failures: 0 of 1,968 previously unscored sites get a score with the fixed code, and no SpliceAI chunk failed. Run: spliceai_unscored_sample_20261110 (exit 0, 1.4 h).
- Why they stay unscored: none of them lies inside a gene of SpliceAI's own gene table (the grch38.txt shipped with the spliceai package). SpliceAI then skips the site on purpose and logs nothing, which is what the old cache recorded. Past tables need no fix.
- Side finding for you to judge: 90 of the 2,000 sites are in genes missing from that table (e.g. SHANK2, TCF4, PDE4DIP). They still get Illumina's precomputed score through VEP (all ≤ 0.05 here), but never the wide-window (-D 4999) local score. Worth a proposal to count panel genes missing from SpliceAI's table?
- To check: TODO.md checklist step 6.

tasks.title: Add SpliceAI2 precomputed scores (informational)
VEP: stop the run when a plugin fails to load
tasks.desc:
Why: without --safe, VEP only warns when a plugin fails to compile or load (Runner.pm:886-915 in the container) and goes on. That plugin's columns then disappear without an error; for UTRAnnotator, every row becomes UTRAnnotator_status=not_annotated.

Proposal: add --safe to the VEP call, or check after VEP that the CSQ header has every expected plugin field and fail the task if one is missing.

Done when: a run with a broken plugin fails, and a normal fixture run still passes. Needs one cluster fixture run.
